cases.excerpt: Between 2007 and 2009, 250 newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed ccRCC cases and 299 sex-, age-matched healthy controls provided complete information including consumption of tea and alcohol, smoking, occupational exposure, body mass index (BMI), hypertension, diabetes, and urolithiasis by face-to-face interview in Shanghai.

comparison.excerpt: Green tea intake (≥500 ml/d) was inversely associated with ccRCC risk

confidence_interval.excerpt: Green tea intake (≥500 ml/d) was inversely associated with ccRCC risk, with an AOR of 0.34 (95% CI 0.21-0.55).

design.excerpt: We carried out a hospital-based case-control study

effect_size.excerpt: Adjusted odds ratio (AOR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were derived through multivariate logistic regression. Green tea intake (≥500 ml/d) was inversely associated with ccRCC risk, with an AOR of 0.34 (95% CI 0.21-0.55).

sample_size.excerpt: We carried out a hospital-based case-control study to examine the effects of health status, lifestyle, and some genetic polymorphisms on ccRCC risk in Chinese subjects.
